arxiv-2208-13533.title: Nearest-neighbour correlation functions for the supersymmetric XYZ spin chain and Painlevé VI Thanks: The first author acknowledges support from the Fonds de la Recherche Scientifique (F.R.S.-FNRS) and the Wetenschappeleijk Onderzoek-Vlanderen (FWO) through the Belgian Excellence of Science (EOS) pr
arxiv-2208-13533.creator: Christian Hagendorf, Hjalmar Rosengren
arxiv-2208-13533.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Christian Hagendorf, Hjalmar Rosengren. We study nearest-neighbour correlation functions for the ground state of the supersymmetric XYZ spin chain with odd length and periodic boundary conditions. Under a technical assumption related to the Q Q -operator of the corresponding eight-vertex model, we show that they can be expressed exactly in terms of the Painlevé VI tau functions s n s_{n} and s ¯ n \bar{s}_{n} introduced by Bazhanov and Mangazeev.

arxiv-2303-17225.title: FreeSeg: Unified, Universal and Open-Vocabulary Image Segmentation
arxiv-2303-17225.creator: Jie Qin, Jie Wu, Pengxiang Yan, Ming Li, Ren Yuxi, Xuefeng Xiao, Yitong Wang, Rui Wang, Shilei Wen, Xin Pan, Xingang Wang
arxiv-2303-17225.description: Abstract Recently, open-vocabulary learning has emerged to accomplish segmentation for arbitrary categories of text-based descriptions, which popularizes the segmentation system to more general-purpose application scenarios. However, existing methods devote to designing specialized architectures or parameters for specific segmentation tasks. These customized design paradigms lead to fragmentation between various segmentation tasks, thus hindering the uniformity of segmentation models.

arxiv-2305-14886.title: How Graph Convolutions Amplify Popularity Bias for Recommendation?
arxiv-2305-14886.creator: Jiajia CHEN, Jiancan WU, Jiawei CHEN, Xin XIN, Yong LI, *
arxiv-2305-14886.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jiajia CHEN, Jiancan WU, Jiawei CHEN, Xin XIN, Yong LI, *. Graph convolutional networks (GCNs) have become prevalent in recommender system (RS) due to their superiority in modeling collaborative patterns. Although improving the overall accuracy, GCNs unfortunately amplify popularity bias — tail items are less likely to be recommended. This effect prevents the GCN-based RS from making precise and fair recommendations, decreasing the effectiveness of recommender systems in the long run.

arxiv-2412-14830.title: Rydberg states and new resonant states of the imidogen molecule NH: pathways for nitrogen release
arxiv-2412-14830.creator: Raju Ghosh 1,2, Binayak Samaddar Choudhuryt 2, János Zsolt Mezei 3,4, Ioan F. Schneider 4,5, Nicolina Pop 6, Kalyan Chakrabarti 7
arxiv-2412-14830.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Raju Ghosh 1,2, Binayak Samaddar Choudhuryt 2, János Zsolt Mezei 3,4, Ioan F. Schneider 4,5, Nicolina Pop 6, Kalyan Chakrabarti 7. Neutral resonant states of molecules play a very important role in the dissociation dynamics and other electronic processes that occur via intermediate capture into these states. With the goal of identifying resonant states, and their corresponding widths, of the imidogen molecule NH as a function of internuclear distance, we have performed detailed R -matrix calculations on the e + NH + system.

arxiv-2501-08056.title: Separating Altermagnetic and Ferromagnetic Effects in X-ray Magnetic Dichroism of Rutile NiF 2
arxiv-2501-08056.creator: A. Hariki, K. Sakurai, T. Okauchi, J. Kuneš
arxiv-2501-08056.description: Abstract We present numerical simulations of x-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) at the L 2 , 3 L_{2,3} edge of Ni in the weakly ferromagnetic altermagnet NiF 2 . Our results predict a significant XMCD signal for light propagating perpendicular to the magnetic moments, which are approximately aligned along the [100] easy-axis direction.

arxiv-2502-11624.title: High-Temperature Superconductivity from Finite-Range Attractive Interaction
arxiv-2502-11624.creator: Dmitry Miserev, 1∗ Joel Hutchinson, 1 Herbert Schoeller, 2 Jelena Klinovaja, 1 and Daniel Loss
arxiv-2502-11624.description: Abstract In this letter we consider D D -dimensional interacting Fermi liquids, and demonstrate that an attractive interaction with a finite range R s R_{s} that is much greater than the Fermi wavelength λ F \lambda_{F} breaks the conventional BCS theory of superconductivity.

arxiv-2510-03680.title: Rainbow Padding: Mitigating Early Termination in Instruction-Tuned Diffusion LLMs
arxiv-2510-03680.creator: ​Bumjun Kim Dongjae Jeon Dueun Kim, Wonje Jeung Albert No
arxiv-2510-03680.description: Abstract Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) have emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive models, offering flexible generation orders and strong performance on complex reasoning tasks. However, instruction-tuned dLLMs exhibit a critical vulnerability we term <eos> overflow: as allocated sequence length increases, responses paradoxically become shorter, collapsing into early termination or degenerating into streams of <eos> tokens.

pmc-10596720.title: Progress on drinking water, sanitation and hygiene in schools: global overview on the WASH programme
pmc-10596720.creator: V Baltag
pmc-10596720.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). ContextSafe drinking-water, sanitation and hygiene are crucial to human health and well-being. Safe WASH is not only a prerequisite to health, but contributes to livelihoods, school attendance and dignity and helps to create resilient communities living in healthy environments. WHO and UNICEF, through the WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP), produce internationally comparable estimates of progress on drinking water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) and are responsible for monitoring the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) targets related to WASH.

pmc-11488075.title: Sex Differences in Human Brain Structure at Birth
pmc-11488075.creator: Yumnah T. Khan, Alex Tsompanidis, Marcin A. Radecki, Lena Dorfschmidt, Yumnah T. Khan, Yumnah T. Khan, Alex Tsompanidis, Marcin A. Radecki, Deep Adhya, Bonnie Ayeung, Rosie Bamford, Tal Biron-Shental, Graham Burton, Wendy Cowell, Jonathan Davies, Dorothea L. Floris, Alice Franklin, Lidia Gabis, Dani
pmc-11488075.description: BackgroundSex differences in human brain anatomy have been well-documented, though remain significantly underexplored during early development. The neonatal period is a critical stage for brain development and can provide key insights into the role that prenatal and early postnatal factors play in shaping sex differences in the brain.

pmc-12564367.title: Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease: Real-World Insights from a Tertiary Care Center
pmc-12564367.creator: Ahmed S. Alanazi, Ahmed A. Alanazi, Abdalrhman Alanizi, Ranad Babalghaith, Reema Alotaibi, Mohammed Alnuhait, Hatoon Bakhribah
pmc-12564367.description: Simple SummaryTrastuzumab deruxtecan is a new cancer treatment that targets tumors carrying a protein called HER2. It has shown great promise for people with advanced cancers, especially breast cancer, but it can sometimes cause a serious lung condition called interstitial lung disease.

pmc-13119029.title: Vitamin D Fortification Strategies and Policy Landscape in Selected European Countries
pmc-13119029.creator: Bartłomiej Czyżniewski, Jolanta Chmielowiec, Krzysztof Chmielowiec, Magdalena Gibas-Dorna
pmc-13119029.description: Background: Vitamin D deficiency remains a widespread public health issue in Europe, despite the availability of sunlight, dietary sources, supplements, and food fortification. National fortification strategies differ substantially in their regulatory approaches, food vehicles, and fortification levels, influencing the population’s vitamin D intake and status.

pmc-13312475.title: scpp5 regulates tooth development and injury-induced repair in zebrafish through mineralization and Wnt/β-catenin signaling
pmc-13312475.creator: Qiqi Liu, Weifeng Hao, Zhenan Zhang, Yu Yue, Deqin Yang
pmc-13312475.description: A member of the secretory calcium-binding phosphoprotein (SCPP) family, scpp5 is specifically expressed in zebrafish tooth germ. Although preliminary data indicates that scpp5 deficiency impairs tooth mineralization, its molecular mechanism and role in tooth repair remain unclear. In this study, we generated scpp5-/- knockout and Tg(hsp70l:scpp5-GFP; cryaa:venus) overexpression zebrafish lines.

pmc-13404305.title: Satisfaction with the quality of early maternity care in the Czech Republic as seen by women - first quantitative results of the nationwide cross-sectional study
pmc-13404305.creator: Radka Wilhelmová, Lenka Veselá, Lukáš Hruban, Michal Pospíšil, Petra Búřilová, Miloslava Kameníková, Andrea Pokorná
pmc-13404305.description: BackgroundWomen's perceptions of satisfaction with maternity care are an integral part of quality assessment in the context of perinatal outcomes in epidemiological data. We present the results of a nationwide project focused on women's satisfaction and experience with standard care covered by public health insurance in the Czech Republic.

pmc-13443946.title: Techno-economic optimization of a hybrid microgrid with integrated backup storage and vehicle-to-grid functionality
pmc-13443946.creator: Noha Nabil Abd-Elhady, Mohammed Fathy Ahmed, Salama Abu-Zaid, Taghreed Said
pmc-13443946.description: This study presents the techno-economic optimization of a hybrid backup system integrated within an off-grid microgrid framework with electric vehicle (EV) grid-interaction capability. A real-world case study from a remote region in Egypt is used to evaluate system performance under realistic operating conditions.

pmc-13505132.title: Computational analysis and automated classification of eating disorder discourse on Twitter’s EDTWT community
pmc-13505132.creator: Jace Li, Chuduo Zhang, Anam Nawaz Khan, Hollie Raynor, Xueping Li

pmc-13548272.title: Generational disparities in maternal healthcare: a life-course perspective on social determinants in Kersa, Eastern Ethiopia
pmc-13548272.creator: Afework Tadele, Merga Dheresa, Muluemebet Abera
pmc-13548272.description: IntroductionMaternal mortality remains persistently high in low- and middle-income countries, driven by inequities in access to and use of maternal healthcare. A life-course perspective offers critical insights into the underlying drivers of these disparities, linking historical, social and structural factors across women’s lives to health outcomes.

pmc-13596240.title: Prevalence, characteristics and risk factors for chronic lower-limb oedema in the older population living in the community or in an aged-care home: a systematic review
pmc-13596240.creator: Maree O’connor, Suzanne Kuys, Michael Steele, Peter Franks, Helen Badge
pmc-13596240.description: IntroductionChronic lower-limb oedema co-occurs with multimorbidity, functional limitations and increased risk of wounds and cellulitis. Findings vary across settings and methodologies.ObjectivesTo synthesise the prevalence, characteristics and risk factors for chronic lower-limb oedema in older adults living in the community or aged-care homes.MethodsA systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

pmc-13678339.title: Direct Transport to a Comprehensive Stroke Center May Offer Outcome Benefits in Metropolitan Thrombectomy Networks
pmc-13678339.creator: Péter Orosz, Zoltán Kővári, Henriette Mészáros, Álmos Hunor Bata, Balázs Kis, Máté Pásztor, Péter Pál Böjti, Loránd Erőss, István Szikora, Béla Merkely, Zsolt Berentei, Ákos Kornfeld, Máté Kondor, Sándor Nardai
pmc-13678339.description: Background and PurposeThe optimal prehospital transport strategy for patients eligible for mechanical thrombectomy remains debated. We evaluated how direct versus secondary transfer to a comprehensive stroke center (CSC) influences outcomes in a large metropolitan stroke network.MethodsThis prospective registry-based cohort study included all patients undergoing thrombectomy between 2015 and 2022 in a city of 1.7 million inhabitants.
